label: Late in the episode, stays higher at D2 after choosing a1 and when S1 is believed good.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * np.square(ep_trial) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * np.square(ep_trial) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * np.square(ep_trial)
terms: (phase == D1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0)**2 ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D2) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1) * ep_dec**2
explanation: Update gate z46 sits near 1 and decays late in the episode, sharply at D2. Timing explains R^2 0.92. What is left is small and grows with episode time. At D2 it is higher after an a1 choice (this trial, observed at D2) and when the ideal observer favours S1 (belief_lo). At D1 it is slightly lower after a previous a1 choice, and at GO it is lower after a2->S1. Rewards and the trial pattern matter little. These effects scale roughly with ep_trial^2 because the gate only moves away from 1 late in the episode. The free fit adds finer within-decile timing terms (ramps after trial 70/80), which account for much of its extra R^2. Those terms are timing rather than task content. Its worst misses are whole late-episode windows where the decay starts earlier or later than the fit predicts.
